text.p: SmithKline Beecham Biologicals said Monday it has recently completed a pivotal phase 3 trial of a vaccine designed to protect against Lyme disease. The trial enrolled about 11,000 persons in New England, the mid-Atlantic region, and the Midwest.
The company said it was releasing the statement in response to queries from the media and the investment community concerning its development of a vaccine against Lyme disease.

It said data from the trial have been reviewed by an independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board. On the basis of that review, the DSMB has recommended that trial participants who previously received placebo now be vaccinated, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has been informed of that recommendation.
Offering vaccinations to placebo-treated patients following a preliminary assessment of the results is stipulated by the trial protocol.
As a result of the findings in the trial, SB intends to file a Product License Application with the FDA this year. The findings will be disclosed through a peer-reviewed publication.
Lyme disease is transmitted by the bite of ticks infected with Borrelia burgdorferi, the organism that causes Lyme disease. If treated early with antibiotics, the disease can be cured.
